source.title: On two open problems on the normality of bent functions

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function in 8 variables whose algebraic degree is 4?

evidence.quote: Do non-normal bent functions in 8 variables and degree 4 exist?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function belonging to the class denoted PS−∖PS_ap?

evidence.quote: Do non-normal bent functions in the PS−∖PS_{ap} class exist?

trace.notes: Normalized the original input as the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/7953868. Direct browser access to the zbMATH URL did not expose readable source text, and local shell network access could not resolve api.zbmath.org. Local resolver metadata in outputs/shards/open-problems-shard-0.csv identified the same work and DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2024.08.023. Exact-work search recovered ScienceDirect and University of Twente records matching that title and DOI; the University of Twente HTML record was selected because it preserved the complete problem statements and class notation.

Mapped the selected HTML source: title and authors; abstract containing the two open problems and an explicit statement that both are resolved; bibliographic metadata with pages, journal, volume, DOI, and publication date; keywords including Boolean bent function, normality, and partial spread class; access-to-document links; and citation exports. The only explicit open-problem region in the readable HTML is the abstract.

Extracted the first explicitly numbered open problem from the abstract: existence of non-normal bent functions in 8 variables and degree 4. The same abstract states that the article resolves both listed problems.

Extracted the second explicitly numbered open problem from the abstract: existence of non-normal bent functions in the PS−∖PS_{ap} class. The same abstract states that the article resolves both listed problems.
Rewrote the compact source question into a standalone existence question while preserving the supported properties: non-normal, Boolean bent, 8 variables, and degree 4.
Rewrote the compact source question into a standalone existence question while preserving the supported PS−∖PS_ap class notation without adding unsupported structural definitions of the class.
No near-duplicate accepted candidate found; kept separate because the source lists it as a distinct numbered open problem about a specific PS class.

Passed self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, solved-status, and schema gates. Marked is_solved=true because the source explicitly says both listed problems are resolved.
